standard.title: Health strategies and resources
standard.description: plan and implement strategies, using health resources, to enhance their own and others' health, safety, relationships and wellbeing
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have analysed how behaviours influence the health, safety, relationships and wellbeing of individuals and communities (Y5-6). They can analyse behavioural influence but have not yet been expected to plan and implement strategies using specific health resources to produce health enhancement outcomes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students plan and implement strategies using health resources to enhance their own and others' health, safety, relationships and wellbeing.

nodes.label: Identifying health needs and relevant resources
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify specific health, safety or wellbeing needs relevant to themselves or their peer group and locate health resources relevant to addressing those needs.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one health, safety or wellbeing need and locate at least one health resource relevant to addressing it.
nodes.typical_width: Identify health needs across multiple domains (nutrition, physical activity, mental health, digital wellbeing, sexual health, preventive practices); locate and assess relevant resources from multiple sources; evaluate resource quality and relevance.
wider: Investigate how First Nations Australians have developed complete diets meeting nutritional requirements and used food for medicinal purposes, and examine how this knowledge connects to understanding health resources more broadly

Research how different cultural traditions value mind-body-spirit connections to health (e.g. Dadirri from First Nations communities of the Daly River region; yoga and meditation from the Asian region) and evaluate their relevance as health resources

response_modes.reason: Health resource identification across multiple domains builds the breadth students need to plan strategies that address the full scope of the descriptor (health, safety, relationships, wellbeing).

success_criteria: Identifies at least one specific health, safety or wellbeing need
Locates at least one health resource relevant to addressing that need

nodes.label: Planning health enhancement strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a strategy to enhance health, safety or wellbeing for themselves or others, incorporating relevant health resources and realistic implementation steps.
nodes.minimum_width: Plan one strategy to enhance health, safety or wellbeing that incorporates at least one health resource and identifies at least one implementation step.
nodes.typical_width: Plan strategies across multiple health domains; use health guidelines (e.g. Australian Guide to Healthy Eating, physical activity guidelines) to inform plans; ensure plans are realistic and achievable; design plans for both personal and others-focused outcomes.
wider: Design a preventive health promotion plan targeting a health practice relevant to young people, drawing on research evidence and community health resources

Investigate food-serving recommendations from the Australian Guide to Healthy Eating and design a practical guide to help students make healthier choices in a specific real-world context (e.g. school canteen)
nodes.hinge_reason: Implementation quality depends on planning quality — students who produce vague or resource-disconnected plans will be unable to implement strategically and will not achieve the enhancement outcomes the descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Scaffold planning with a consistent structure: identify the need, identify the resource, design the strategy, predict the outcome, identify implementation steps. Without structure, plans tend to be aspirational without being actionable.

success_criteria: Plans a strategy to enhance health, safety or wellbeing
Incorporates at least one health resource in the plan
Identifies at least one realistic implementation step

nodes.label: Implementing and evaluating strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can implement a health enhancement strategy and evaluate its impact on their own or others' health, safety, relationships or wellbeing.
nodes.minimum_width: Implement one health enhancement strategy and describe at least one observed or expected impact on health, safety, relationships or wellbeing.
nodes.typical_width: Implement and evaluate strategies across multiple health domains; evaluate nutritional value, sustainability and other criteria relevant to specific strategies; assess impact on health outcomes; propose adjustments based on evaluation findings.
wider: Implement health promotion activities targeting preventive health practices for young people and evaluate their impact on attitudes or behaviours within a school or community context
Investigate tools and design routines that help regulate digital environment use and ensure healthy patterns — implementing and evaluating the design in their own daily context
Examine how different approaches to promoting positive mental health (mindfulness, relaxation, healthy eating) compare in effectiveness, and develop a personal plan incorporating multiple strategies

response_modes.reason: Implementation and evaluation integrates needs identification, resource knowledge and planning into action and reflection — instruction should scaffold the full plan-implement-evaluate cycle as a connected process.

success_criteria: Implements a planned health enhancement strategy
Evaluates at least one impact of the strategy on health, safety, relationships or wellbeing
Identifies at least one way the strategy could be refined based on the evaluation
